items.text: Correction to Saturday's item: Sky's own team sheet for Forest v Spurs lists Igor Jesus among the substitutes and shows him coming on in the 59th minute, alongside Daniel Munoz - he was not left out of the squad, and Chris Wood came on separately at 74. The real change is that he has lost his starting place: he started GW1 and GW2 and Liam Delap led the line on Saturday. The model still rates him the best free-agent forward available at 11.8 over the next five.

Barcola finally got his first Liverpool start tonight, in the Champions League against Atletico Madrid, then went down clutching his calf in the 58th minute and had to be replaced - ESPN's live commentary called it a spell that 'doesn't look great' for him. After three weeks of single-cameo minutes, this is a fresh fitness question rather than the pure selection one this week's claim was built on, and it pushes his path into the Premier League XI further away, not closer.

Ben Chilwell has re-signed for Crystal Palace and scored the winner at Fulham with his first touch, having come on for Tyrick Mitchell on 73 minutes. Mitchell scored both of Palace's other goals and is the pick of the free-agent defenders this week, but Chilwell plays his position and is now in the building - one to watch rather than a reason to pass.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola confirmed Barcola's exit at the hour mark against Atletico Madrid was cramp, not an injury, saying he is 'very happy' with the forward's first start and two clear second-half chances on goal. That corrects last night's 'doesn't look great' read, though it changes nothing about the underlying case: Barcola still has zero Premier League minutes started this season and faces Gakpo, Isak and Ngumoha for a place at Fulham on Saturday.

Iraola told Friday's press conference that Barcola's cramp is not an injury and he 'should be available' for Saturday's Fulham game if training goes to plan - a likely second Liverpool start. The model still has him at just 0.16 availability and 2.4 next5, the same blind spot every marquee mid-season arrival runs into: it cannot see a player easing into a new team, only a name with no minutes.

Tottenham's own site confirms James Maddison is back in Roberto De Zerbi's plans and Mohammed Kudus - who can play 'as a winger, as a number 10, as a striker up front' - is 'very close to being ready to start', while Mykhailo Mudryk has been ruled out six to eight weeks with an ankle injury from his Forest debut. One rival for Marmoush's central role has gone, but two more are converging on the same weekend.

Free agent Jannik Schuster made his Premier League debut replacing the injured Nathan Collins on Saturday, and Brentford's own site quotes Keith Andrews saying part of the decision to let Ethan Pinnock leave was confidence in Schuster's ability - he 'was thrown into it today and he produced.' The model has him at just 0.31 availability off a single appearance, the same blind spot that undersells every new arrival.

Strand Larsen scored twice in Tuesday's Carabao Cup win over Middlesbrough, per Crystal Palace's own match report, strengthening his case to lead the line at home to Ipswich today with Mateta still out - a firmer position than last week's bench role behind Nketiah, though no permitted outlet has published today's confirmed XI yet.

Confirmed: Strand Larsen leads the line again for Palace against Ipswich this afternoon, with Tyrick Mitchell at wing-back - Crystal Palace's own team news has Nketiah failing his pre-match fitness test after 'we knew he was a doubt', resolving this morning's open question in Strand Larsen's favour.

Barcola starts for Liverpool against Fulham this afternoon, his second start in four days after Tuesday's Champions League appearance against Atletico - Liverpool's own site confirms it, with Iraola turning to him again on the left. The model still has him buried at avail 0.26 and next5 3.5 off zero career games in its sample, well behind what two straight starts for a fit forward should be worth.

Newcastle's deadline-day arrival Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a reported 51m signing from Lille, is "getting closer to starting" according to boss Matthias Jaissle ahead of the Leeds trip, having so far only appeared from the bench against Bournemouth. The model still rates him bottom of the free-agent forward board at 0.19 availability and a 2.7-point next5 off zero Premier League games - the same blind spot that undersold Barcola for weeks.

Milenkovic and Cunha both started Forest's full 90 minutes in Saturday's 2-1 win at Aston Villa, Igor Jesus scoring an 88th-minute winner - this week's recurring hamstring doubt did not materialize. The model's 0.60 availability for Milenkovic looks conservative; the Hill-for-Milenkovic waiver claim now rests on fixture value alone, not fitness.

Correction to last night's report: ESPN's own live commentary shows Milenkovic and Cunha did not play Saturday's 2-1 win at Villa Park - both dropped out with hamstring tightness found in Friday's training, Diomande and Munoz starting in their place. Glasner expects Milenkovic to also miss the Coventry game, with a return targeted for the fixture after.

Bogle scored in Leeds' 4-1 demolition of Newcastle on Monday night, netting in the 34th minute as part of a 3-0 half-time lead, per Newcastle's own match centre. The model's next5 figure for him (12.6) is built on fixtures and form, not tonight's goal, so treat this as a point in his favour that the board hasn't priced in yet.

Newcastle's 51m deadline-day signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo got his full first-team debut in that same Leeds game, but Jaissle hooked him at the 57th minute with the score already 3-0, per the club's own match centre. The model still rates him bottom of the forward pool off essentially no minutes (avail 0.19, next5 2.7) - a real data point at last, though one bad afternoon does not settle whether he starts again against Bournemouth.

Mohammed Kudus made his first Tottenham start since January in Wednesday's Carabao Cup exit at Liverpool, but Marmoush also started and played the full 90 in a heavily rotated XI - the pecking order for Justin's forward has not shifted yet, though Kudus's return is a fresh name to watch.

Maresca left Haaland and Gvardiol out of Manchester City's squad entirely for tonight's Carabao Cup tie with Norwich - Man City's own site frames it as workload rotation after Sunday's derby, not injury, with both expected back for Sunday's league game at home to Sunderland. Worth knowing before a blank appearance tonight reads as a fitness concern on the board.

Adrien Truffert, this week's top waiver target for Justin's defence, has earned his first call-up to the senior France squad, per Bournemouth's own site - recognition for a player who started all 38 league games last season and is in career-best form now. It doesn't change the case for claiming him, just reinforces it.

Anton Stach, Justin's rank-3 GW6 waiver target, has been named in Jurgen Klopp's first Germany squad on the back of an eye-catching debut season at Leeds - a form signal for a player already on the claims board as the upgrade on Lewis-Potter, not a change to his role at the club.

Raya started as normal in goal for Arsenal's 3-0 defeat at Brighton today (Gross, Kostoulas, Chema Andres) - the loss is on the defense in front of him, not a fitness issue, and a clean team sheet finally retires the recurring 'knee bandaged' Raya injury story that has resurfaced and been discarded on four separate runs since 5 September.

Free agent Pascal Gross scored the opener in Brighton's 3-0 win over Arsenal today, with Kostoulas adding a second before half-time - live evidence for the model's own suggested Gross-for-Barcola swap (+15.1 next5), which this week's claims board again declined given Barcola's own two straight Liverpool starts.

Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage said this week he hopes Mateta and Dean Henderson will return only 'after the international break,' pushing his striker's timeline further out than earlier estimates and cementing Strand Larsen as Palace's clear starting forward through the whole GW6 waiver window.

Leeds' own team news for today's home game against Crystal Palace has Bogle among the substitutes, the first time all season a permitted source has actually left him out of the XI - James Justin comes in at right wing-back, with Joe Rodon and Jaka Bijol both restored to the back three. The model's 0.89 availability figure has not caught up with it yet.

Sunderland's deadline-day signing of Malick Fofana from Lyon, a deal worth up to GBP30m that owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus personally flew to Lyon to close after Crystal Palace tried to hijack it, is the same blind spot that hit Barcola and Munoz: the model has him at just 0.15 availability and a 2.1 next5, near the bottom of the free-agent midfield pool. He has only started for Sunderland in the Carabao Cup so far and has yet to nail down a Premier League place.

Leeds' own match report confirms Jayden Bogle started and was booked in today's 0-0 draw with Crystal Palace, contradicting this morning's substitutes report - he was not benched after all, undercutting part of this week's Truffert-for-Bogle case.

Jan Paul Van Hecke's stoppage-time header was Tottenham's only bright spot in Sunday's 2-3 home defeat to Aston Villa, which leaves Spurs winless with two points from five games, in the relegation zone, and reportedly piling pressure on manager Roberto De Zerbi.

Adrien Truffert, this week's claim-2 waiver target, started again for Bournemouth and picked out Evanilson's early flick that Alisson somehow kept out, in today's 0-1 home defeat to Liverpool in which Alexander Isak scored the winner on his return to Vitality Stadium.

Brian Brobbey, this week's rank-3 waiver target, was taken off after just 35 minutes of Netherlands' 1-1 draw with Germany tonight, pulling up and pointing to his right leg four days after his Man City hat-trick - no diagnosis yet, but it puts real doubt on that claim before the 9 October waiver close.

Jayden Bogle has been named among the Premier League's eight nominees for September's Player of the Month award, the League's own nominee page crediting his goal in the 1-1 draw at Brighton and a starring role in the 4-1 demolition of Newcastle, with Leeds boasting the joint-tightest defence in the league alongside Everton. It is the strongest evidence yet against dropping him for Truffert, a swap this board has considered and set aside three weeks running.

Kevin Schade has joined Bogle and Gross as a nominee for the Premier League's September Player of the Month award, Brentford's own site confirming two goals in three unbeaten league games (Sunderland, Bournemouth, Chelsea); voting closes Monday. A third of Justin's or his waiver targets' players is now up for the award this month, and none of the three has a fitness question against him.

Bournemouth's Alex Scott (yours) withdrew from England duty with a tendon injury picked up against Croatia and could miss 'several weeks' per Sky Sports; scans planned. The model still has him at 50% availability and 15.4 next5, which is far too kind - a replacement claim is now live (Anderson is the model's pick).

Haaland (yours) asked to be taken off after 67 minutes of Norway's 2-1 loss to Portugal, a week before Man City host Liverpool; his coach said the plan was to play him until he could no longer contribute. No injury has been reported, but watch City's pre-match news.

Tavernier (yours) may inherit Bournemouth penalty duty: the Premier League's Scout notes regular takers Kluivert and Kroupi are both injured, and Tavernier leads midfielders with three open-play goals. Chelsea away in GW6 is the test; the model has him at 18.5 next5, the second-best in your midfield.

Barcola (yours) has a clearer route into Liverpool's XI for Sunday's game with Man City: the Premier League's Matchweek 6 preview has Isak and Gakpo confirmed out and Ekitike still sidelined, with Lewis Koumas or Barcola himself as the option up front. The model's 0.36 availability for him reads as a squad-fringe player and does not see Liverpool's forward injuries.

Van Hecke (yours) is fit for Spurs at Old Trafford despite a knock with the Netherlands, De Zerbi confirmed, but his wife gave birth to twins on Thursday and the manager says he has to consider the 'emotional aspect'. Treat his start as a genuine call rather than the model's 1.00 certainty.

Schade (yours) is back on the grass but not cleared: Keith Andrews said "we'll have to see how much" he and Jannik Schuster can play against Liverpool after their injuries at Villa. Treat the model's 0.69 availability as the ceiling, and keep a bench cover in mind for tomorrow's 3pm kick-off.

Brobbey (yours) is 'ready' per Regis Le Bris, and with Wilson Isidor being assessed day by day for a minor injury, the Premier League says it is unclear who leads Sunderland's line at Bournemouth. That is a better path to a start than the model's 0.90 availability suggests, though he has not started since the Netherlands hamstring problem.

Haaland (yours) limped down the tunnel after full time in City's 3-2 win over Ipswich on Saturday, per Sky Sports; Enzo Maresca said "nothing serious" but added "we will see", and listed Kovacic and Nico O'Reilly among others with knocks. The model has him at 0.73 availability and the top next5 on your squad, so watch City's pre-match news before the GW8 deadline.

Brian Brobbey (Justin) missed Sunderland's 2-0 defeat at Bournemouth with his hamstring problem, though he has trained with the squad this week and Le Bris is reported hopeful of a return next week. That is consistent with the 75% flag and the model's 0.52 availability, but with Sunderland also in Europa League action Thursday, a start before the GW8 deadline is far from certain.

Schade (yours) looks set to reclaim a starting place at Hull this weekend: the Premier League's GW8 Scout says his shoulder injury limited him to a 45-minute substitute role against Liverpool, and that he should be ready to start. That supports the model's 1.00 availability for him, so no cover is needed unless Brentford's pre-match news says otherwise.

runs.note: Evening sweep ~13 hours after this morning's 08:06 run, still inside the three-week international break with no squad-club fixtures played since. 18 searches via a research pass plus 2 direct club-site checks: club-by-club on every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Tottenham, Brighton, Man City, Liverpool, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) and shortlist club Sunderland, plus general PL injury and fixtures-resuming sweeps. Nothing cleared the sourcing bar as new. Re-caught and discarded the recurring Sky Sports 'Pickford out for a month, thigh injury' story a third time - fetched the article directly and its own datePublished field again reads 7 September 2022, not this season. Checked brightonandhovealbion.com's own news feed directly for a Gross injury story surfaced only via an unpermitted aggregator (claiming he was ruled out v Newcastle) - the club's own feed shows nothing but the Arsenal match report already published, so that claim is unconfirmed and not used. Checked safc.com's own news feed directly for Brobbey - no current story either way. Confirmed via permitted sources but not news, since already known and reflected in the squad: Van Hecke's move to Tottenham, Vuskovic's move to Brighton, Strand Larsen's move to Crystal Palace and Fofana's move to Sunderland are all real, completed transfers, not events from the last 24 hours. Truffert's France recall (afcb.co.uk, 18 Sep) and Stach's fit, uncapped-injury Germany squad news (leedsunited.com) both reconfirmed but already published this week. Gvardiol's alleged leg fracture, Haaland's alleged World Cup fatigue and Barcola's Atletico cramp scare all traced only to unpermitted outlets (FOX Sports, CBS Sports, Get French Football News, Yahoo, Sportsmole) with no BBC/Guardian/Sky/ESPN/Reuters/AP or club-site corroboration, so none is used. League position and waiver order unchanged: Justin 2nd of 6 on 252 points, 5th of 6 in the reversed GW6 waiver order. Nothing published; division stays idle for the international break until around 11 October, well ahead of the 9 October waiver close.

First run ~11.5 hours after last night's 21:12 sweep, during the international break with no squad-club football since GW5 ended 20 September and none resuming until around 11 October. Club-by-club pass on every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Brighton, Hull, Tottenham, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) plus free-agent-target clubs (Sunderland, Leeds again for Stach) and two general PL sweeps, about 16 searches. Nothing survived that both moves a verdict and clears a permitted source. Chased down one lead in depth: cpfc.co.uk's own 'Sage on facing Leeds & international break plans' has the manager differentiate Henderson ('more sure') from Mateta ('more uncertain... best answer in two weeks') for the first time on the post-break return - genuine new detail, but it only restates the existing 'both out past the international break' story with more precision, not a reversal, so left unpublished rather than padding a headline that changes nothing for Strand Larsen. Also checked: Garner (England Nations League call-up, no fitness angle), Raya (Player of the Matchweek for a derby-defining penalty save, plus Spain duty), Stach (clean bill of health on Germany duty), Groß and Kostoulas (both scored again for Brighton against Arsenal on 19 September, already reflected in the 19 September items), Barcola (Iraola praised him ahead of the Bournemouth game but offered no new fact), and Lewis-Potter's wing-back competition with Aaron Hickey (no confirmed change to his starting role). Rayan Cherki's quad injury at Man City is real but he is not a squad or shortlist player. Nothing published.

Second run today, ~12.5 hours after this morning's 08:30 sweep, still inside the international break with no squad-club football since GW5 ended 20 September. Club-by-club pass on every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Hull, Brighton, Tottenham, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) plus free-agent-target club Sunderland and three general PL sweeps (injuries, transfers, Nations League withdrawals), 19 searches. Chased down three leads that looked like fresh injuries but all traced to stale, already-resolved dates once read in full: a Tavernier hamstring story traces to an afcb.co.uk article dated 23 January 2026, a prior-season injury long since recovered from (he's started all five league games this season with no fitness question); a Bogle 'foot injury' story traces to a Wolves match and subsequent Chelsea FA Cup semi-final references, both from last season, resolved before this campaign began; and Stach's 'foot/ankle injury' coverage traces to a laceration sustained against Brighton in May 2026, pre-season, with Leeds' own reporting saying it kept him out only two-three weeks and he has played every league game since. None of the three is current. Also checked and found nothing citable: Brobbey's Man City hat-trick and the Arsenal/Chelsea transfer interest around him (Yahoo, not permitted, and the window closed 1 September regardless); Gvardiol's recurring 'broken leg' story surfaced again and is the same discredited item; a Marmoush/Savinho ESPN piece reads as pre-transfer chatter from before his move actually completed, not current; Van Hecke and Garner both confirmed away with their countries (Netherlands, England) with no injury; Mateta/Strand Larsen coverage on wearepalace.uk is not a permitted source and, read closely, describes pre-season friendlies, not the current hamstring situation already published. Nothing published.

Led with Brian Brobbey's injury substitution in tonight's Netherlands-Germany Nations League draw (Sky Sports live blog, 20:44 UTC), confirmed independently via ESPN's own match data (subbed 35', 11 touches, no goals) - material because he is this week's rank-3 waiver target. Full club-by-club sweep on every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Hull, Tottenham, Brighton, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) plus free-agent shortlist club Sunderland and general PL injury/transfer sweeps, ~18 searches. One other lead chased and discarded: a 'Kevin Schade set for surgery, out for months' story is the same September 2023 adductor injury (recovered by April 2024), not current. Everything else reconfirmed unchanged: Stach, Bogle, Ajayi, Van Hecke, Gvardiol, Haaland, Vuskovic, Groß, Tzolakis and Truffert all fit and undisturbed on international duty or at their clubs.

Morning sweep during the international break (GW6 fixtures resume 10 October, waivers close 9 October). Full club-by-club pass on every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Hull, Tottenham, Brighton, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) plus free-agent shortlist clubs (Sunderland, Hull for Tzolakis) and general PL injury/fixtures sweeps, 20 searches. Chased the one open thread from last night in depth: fetched Sky Sports' own Netherlands 1-1 Germany match report directly, which confirms in its own words that Brobbey was 'taken off with what appeared to be a hamstring injury' - firmer sourcing than last night's live-blog citation, but still no diagnosis or timeline from Sunderland, so claim 3 stays at low confidence rather than being upgraded or downgraded further. Also checked and found nothing citable: Stach came on for 26 minutes off the bench for Germany against the Netherlands (leedsunited.com), fit but a squad option internationally, no change to his Leeds status; a Pascal Gross 'ruled out, undisclosed injury' story attributes the quote to Fabian Hurzeler, who is not Brighton's manager, and is directly contradicted by Gross scoring and starting against Arsenal five days ago, so discarded as stale and wrong; Pickford, Raya, Bogle, Ajayi, Van Hecke, Vuskovic, Haaland, Barcola, Lewis-Potter, Schade, Scott, Tavernier, Truffert and Tzolakis all reconfirmed fit and undisturbed; Gvardiol's recurring 'broken leg' story resurfaced again and is again the same discredited item, contradicted by his own recent minutes; Mateta and Henderson both still out, already known and reflected in Strand Larsen's nailed status. League position unchanged: Justin 2nd of 6 on 252 points, 5th of 6 in the reversed GW6 waiver order. Nothing published.

Evening sweep ~12.5 hours after this morning's 08:35 run, still inside the international break (GW6 fixtures resume 10 October, waivers close 9 October). Club-by-club pass on every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Hull, Tottenham, Brighton, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) plus free-agent shortlist clubs (Sunderland, Brighton for Gross, Leeds for Stach) and general PL injury/transfer sweeps, 18 searches. Nothing cleared the sourcing bar as new. Re-checked Brobbey directly against Sky Sports' and Sunderland's own coverage of last Thursday's Netherlands 1-1 Germany draw: Xavi Hernandez has confirmed Brobbey is injured and returned to Wearside, but no club or permitted outlet has published a diagnosis or timeline yet, so claim 3 stays unchanged at low confidence rather than moving either way. Stach reconfirmed fit and undisturbed via Sky Sports' own recent Forest match report (matchwinner with a late free-kick) - no ankle issue, the injury story surfacing again is the same stale pre-transfer 2025 item. The recurring Pascal Gross 'ruled out by Fabian Hurzeler' story resurfaced again in search results and was discarded again for the same reason as every prior run: contradicted by his own goal and start against Arsenal on the 19th, with no permitted outlet reporting an injury since. The recurring Gvardiol 'broken leg' and Pickford 'thigh injury, out a month' stories both resurfaced again and are again the same discredited 2022/prior-season items, contradicted by both players' own current minutes. Reconfirmed unchanged and not news: Raya, Bogle, Ajayi, Van Hecke, Vuskovic, Haaland, Barcola, Lewis-Potter, Schade, Scott, Tavernier and Truffert all fit; Marmoush still Tottenham's starting striker; Mateta and Henderson both still out for Palace past the break, already reflected in Strand Larsen's nailed status. League position unchanged: Justin 2nd of 6 on 252 points, 5th of 6 in the reversed GW6 waiver order. Nothing published.

Morning sweep ~11 hours after last night's 21:06 run, still inside the international break (GW6 fixtures resume 10 October, waivers close 9 October). Club-by-club pass on every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Hull, Tottenham, Brighton, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) plus free-agent shortlist clubs (Sunderland for Brobbey) and general PL sweeps, 18 searches plus two direct-fetch verifications. Chased the one open thread in depth: ESPN's own international-break injury roundup confirms Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said 'Brian is indeed injured' after Thursday's game and that Joshua Zirkzee has replaced him in the squad - but it gives no weeks-out estimate. Several non-permitted outlets (TeamTalk, Sunderland Echo, LiveScore, 101 Great Goals) are running a 'Le Bris says two to four weeks' quote, but a safc.com site search turns up no matching article, and one version of the same quote wrongly attributes the injury to 'last weekend's defeat to Fulham' rather than Thursday's Netherlands game - a sign of quote contamination with an older injury, not a fresh diagnosis - so it is not used here and claim 3 stays at low confidence rather than being sharpened either way. Also checked and found nothing citable: Pickford and Garner both fit and in Thomas Tuchel's England squad (already known, no injury angle); Kostoulas took stitches for Greece but is not considered serious; Vuskovic's Man Utd cramp scare confirmed as nothing; Bogle, Ajayi, Van Hecke, Gvardiol, Haaland, Groß, Schade, Lewis-Potter, Scott, Tavernier and Truffert all reconfirmed fit and undisturbed with nothing new. Nothing published.

Evening sweep ~13 hours after this morning's 08:07 run, still the international break (GW6 fixtures resume 10 October, waivers close 9 October). Club-by-club pass on every squad club plus free-agent shortlist clubs (Sunderland for Brobbey, Brighton for Gross, Leeds for Stach, Bournemouth for Truffert, Hull for Tzolakis) and general sweeps on De Zerbi's position at Tottenham, Mateta's return timeline at Palace and Man City internationals, 12 searches plus three direct-fetch verifications (safc.com news index, ESPN's international-break injury roundup, leedsunited.com's Bournemouth-clash presser). Chased Brobbey again: Sky/ESPN's own reporting is unchanged since this morning - Xavi Hernandez's 'indeed injured' quote and the Zirkzee call-up, still no diagnosis or return date from Sunderland itself, and safc.com's own news index carries no new article on him since January. A leedsunited.com press-conference page calling Bogle 'back in team training' after a bruise looked promising but is dated 25 Sep 25, a year stale, and Leeds do not play Wolves this season - discarded. Also discarded on inspection: a recurring Gvardiol 'broken leg' story mixing in an old rehab timeline (same one flagged stale on 24 September) and a De Zerbi sack-pressure story that changes nothing about Marmoush's role since no permitted outlet reports a change to Tottenham's forward line. Everything else reconfirmed unchanged: Pickford, Raya, Bogle, Ajayi, Van Hecke, Vuskovic, Haaland, Barcola, Groß, Stach, Lewis-Potter, Scott, Schade, Tavernier and Truffert. Nothing published.

Led with Jayden Bogle's September Player of the Month nomination, confirmed via premierleague.com's own nominee article (goal at Brighton, starring role in the 4-1 demolition of Newcastle, joint-tightest PL defence with Everton) - the strongest evidence yet for keeping him over the Truffert swap. Pascal Gross also nominated on the same page, reinforcing claim 1's Gross-for-Barcola case. Full club-by-club sweep across all 11 squad clubs (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Hull, Tottenham, Brighton, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) plus free-agent shortlist clubs (Sunderland for Brobbey, Brighton for Gross, Leeds for Stach, Bournemouth for Truffert, Hull for Tzolakis), ~30 searches plus direct-fetch verification on a dozen pages. Several leads chased and discarded once read in full, all resurfacing stale articles rather than fresh news: an arsenal.com 'Raya thigh issue, doubtful for Leicester' story dated 27 Sep 2024 (two years stale, same calendar date coincidence); a Sky Sports 'Guardiola unsure when Haaland will return' story dated 28 Feb 2026, from before this season's transfer window even opened; a brentfordfc.com 'Lewis-Potter out two months, knee injury' story dated 9 Mar 2023, from the Thomas Frank era; the same outlet's Kevin Schade adductor-surgery story, also Thomas Frank-era, already flagged stale on 24 September. Checked safc.com directly for a Brobbey update - its 24 September international round-up carries no mention of him, and no permitted outlet has published a diagnosis since Netherlands duty on the 24th, though the model's own news field has now caught up with a 'hamstring injury, 75% chance of playing' note and cut his availability from 0.90 to 0.68 this week. Everything else reconfirmed unchanged: Pickford, Raya, Ajayi, Van Hecke, Vuskovic, Gvardiol, Haaland, Barcola, Stach, Scott, Schade, Tavernier and Truffert all fit and undisturbed. League position unchanged: Justin 2nd of 6 on 252 points, 5th of 6 in the reversed GW6 waiver order.

Second run today, ~12.5 hours after this morning's 08:35 sweep, still inside the international break (GW6 fixtures resume 10 October, waivers close 9 October). Club-by-club pass on every squad club (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Hull, Tottenham, Brighton, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace) plus free-agent shortlist clubs (Sunderland, Coventry, Ipswich) and general PL/rival sweeps, about 20 searches. Led with brentfordfc.com's own confirmation that Kevin Schade is nominated for September's Player of the Month (two goals in three unbeaten games), a third of Justin's/his targets' players up for the award this month alongside Bogle and Gross. Chased down and discarded several leads that read as fresh but traced to stale or superseded stories on direct fetch: a 'Gvardiol expected to miss the rest of the season with a broken leg' result is last season's January-to-May injury, long since recovered (mancity.com's own reporting has him scoring and assisting again this month); a Tavernier hamstring story traces to an afcb.co.uk piece dated January 2026 and is contradicted by ESPN's own player stats showing him playing 75 minutes in the 20 September Liverpool game; a Bogle 'foot injury, just a bruise' story and a Stach 'ankle injury' story both trace to old leedsunited.com pieces (last season and pre-season respectively), contradicted by today's own Bogle Player of the Month nomination and Stach's ever-present league minutes this season. A 'Brobbey out 2-4 weeks, injured against Fulham' result does not match the established Netherlands-Germany hamstring story and could not be verified at safc.com or any permitted outlet, so not used - claim 3 stays at low confidence with no firmer timeline than already on file. Also checked: Truffert played the full 90 and kept a clean sheet on his France debut in Zidane's first game in charge (reported only via non-permitted outlets so not published, though it reinforces his fitness case); Emersonn's Ipswich form (2 goals in his last two starts, confirmed via ESPN) is real but both games are more than a week old, so held rather than published as news; Alex Scott an unused England substitute against Spain, no fitness concern; Coventry's four free-agent shortlist names (Rushworth, Thomas, Dasilva, Thomas-Asante) are untouched by the club's current injury list. Nothing else moved. League position unchanged: Justin 2nd of 6 on 252 points, 5th of 6 in the reversed GW6 waiver order.

Morning sweep ~11 hours after last night's 21:11 run, still inside the international break (GW6 fixtures resume 10 October, waivers close 9 October). Full club-by-club sweep (Everton, Arsenal, Leeds, Hull, Tottenham, Brighton, Man City, Liverpool, Brentford, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace, Sunderland, Coventry, Fulham, Nottingham Forest) plus today's international-duty injuries, ~25 searches. Nothing cleared the bar. A 'Tavernier hamstring, out at Brighton' story recurred again and was traced directly to afcb.co.uk's own URL date (23 January 2026, last season, a Liverpool-fixture piece) - stale, discarded again.
